title: Mathematics: Unit-wise Objective Question Bank

toc.title: 5.1 Sets, Whole Numbers, Rational and Irrational Numbers
5.2 Ratio, Proportion and the Unitary Method
5.9 Coordinates, Transformation, Tessellation, Bearing and Scale Drawing

html:
In Mathematics the one-mark items are one-step questions: a definition, a formula recalled correctly, a single substitution, a sign. They are also the items most often lost to carelessness rather than to ignorance. This chapter covers all twenty-one units of the Grade 8 textbook, grouped into ten sections. Each section opens with the formulas and facts the one-mark items keep returning to, then gives the items, then a key that shows the single step.

The one-step habit

Before you write anything, ask: which formula is this? Write the formula, substitute, and only then calculate. Nine out of ten lost one-mark items in Mathematics come from substituting into a half-remembered formula.

5.1 Sets, Whole Numbers, Rational and Irrational Numbers

Facts. n(A \cup B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A \cap B). A set with n elements has 2^n subsets. Rational numbers can be written as \frac{p}{q} with q \neq 0; \sqrt{2}, \sqrt{3} and \pi are irrational. Every terminating or recurring decimal is rational. Zero is neither positive nor negative; it is a whole number but not a natural number. 0 has no multiplicative inverse.

  1. If n(A) = 12, n(B) = 9 and n(A \cap B) = 4, then n(A \cup B) is [1]a17b21c25d13
  2. The number of subsets of a set with 4 elements is [1]a4b8c16d32
  3. Which of the following is an irrational number? [1]a0.25b\frac{3}{7}c\sqrt{9}d\sqrt{7}
  4. The smallest whole number is [1]a-1b0c1dthere is none
  5. The additive inverse of -\frac{5}{8} is [1]a\frac{8}{5}b-\frac{8}{5}c\frac{5}{8}d0
  6. If A = \{1,2,3\} and B = \{3,4\}, then A \cap B is [1]a\{1,2,3,4\}b\{3\}c\{1,2\}d\emptyset
  7. The decimal 0.\overline{6} expressed as a fraction is [1]a\frac{6}{10}b\frac{2}{3}c\frac{3}{5}d\frac{6}{11}
  8. Which statement is true? [1]aevery integer is a whole numberbevery whole number is an integercevery rational number is an integerd\sqrt{2} is rational
Answers

1. (a) — 12+9-4 = 17.

2. (c) — 2^4 = 16.

3. (d) — \sqrt{9}=3 is rational; \sqrt{7} is not.

4. (b) — whole numbers start at 0.

5. (c) — the additive inverse changes the sign.

6. (b) — only 3 is common.

7. (b) — 0.\overline{6} = \frac{6}{9} = \frac{2}{3}.

8. (b) — -3 is an integer but not a whole number.

5.2 Ratio, Proportion and the Unitary Method

Facts. In the proportion a:b = c:d, ad = bc. To divide x in the ratio m:n, each share is \frac{m}{m+n}x and \frac{n}{m+n}x. In direct proportion, one quantity rises as the other rises; in inverse proportion, the product stays constant. Mean proportional between a and b is \sqrt{ab}.

  1. If 3:5 = x:20, then x is [1]a10b12c15d4
  2. Rs 480 divided between two friends in the ratio 3:5 gives the smaller share [1]aRs 160bRs 180cRs 240dRs 300
  3. The mean proportional between 4 and 9 is [1]a6b6.5c13d36
  4. If 6 workers build a wall in 10 days, 12 workers of the same capacity will take [1]a20 daysb10 daysc5 daysd2 days
  5. 5 pens cost Rs 125. The cost of 8 such pens is [1]aRs 180bRs 200cRs 225dRs 250
  6. The ratio 45 minutes : 2 hours in its simplest form is [1]a45:2b3:8c9:24d1:3
  7. Which pair is in inverse proportion? [1]anumber of books and their costbspeed and time for a fixed distancecdistance and time at a fixed speeddside and perimeter of a square
  8. If a:b = 2:3 and b:c = 4:5, then a:c is [1]a2:5b8:15c5:8d3:4
Answers

1. (b) — x = \frac{3\times20}{5} = 12.

2. (b) — \frac{3}{8}\times480 = 180.

3. (a) — \sqrt{4\times9} = 6.

4. (c) — inverse proportion: \frac{6\times10}{12} = 5 days.

5. (b) — one pen Rs 25, so 8\times25 = 200.

6. (b) — 45:120 = 3:8.

7. (b) — at fixed distance, speed × time is constant.

8. (b) — a:b:c = 8:12:15, so a:c = 8:15.

5.3 Profit and Loss, Simple Interest

Facts. Profit = S.P. - C.P.; profit per cent = \frac{\text{profit}}{\text{C.P.}}\times100. Discount is always on the marked price; VAT is charged on the price after discount. Simple interest I = \frac{PTR}{100}; amount A = P + I.

  1. An article bought for Rs 800 is sold for Rs 920. The profit per cent is [1]a12 %b15 %c20 %d13 %
  2. A shirt marked Rs 1,200 is sold at 10 % discount. Its selling price is [1]aRs 1,080bRs 1,100cRs 1,020dRs 1,320
  3. The simple interest on Rs 5,000 for 2 years at 8 % per annum is [1]aRs 400bRs 800cRs 1,000dRs 80
  4. If the cost price is Rs 500 and the loss is 12 %, the selling price is [1]aRs 440bRs 480cRs 560dRs 400
  5. Rs 2,000 becomes Rs 2,300 in 3 years at simple interest. The rate per annum is [1]a3 %b5 %c10 %d15 %
  6. VAT at 13 % on a bill of Rs 2,000 is [1]aRs 130bRs 200cRs 260dRs 2,260
  7. Profit per cent is always calculated on the [1]aselling pricebmarked priceccost priceddiscount
  8. In how many years will Rs 4,000 earn Rs 960 as simple interest at 6 % per annum? [1]a2b3c4d5
Answers

1. (b) — profit Rs 120; \frac{120}{800}\times100 = 15 %.

2. (a) — 1200 - 120 = 1080.

3. (b) — \frac{5000\times2\times8}{100} = 800.

4. (a) — 500 - 60 = 440.

5. (b) — I = 300; R = \frac{100\times300}{2000\times3} = 5 %.

6. (c) — 13 % of 2000 = 260.

7. (c) — on the cost price.

8. (c) — T = \frac{100\times960}{4000\times6} = 4 years.

5.4 Area and Volume

Facts. Rectangle A = lb; square A = l^2; triangle A = \frac{1}{2}bh; parallelogram A = bh; trapezium A = \frac{1}{2}(a+b)h; circle A = \pi r^2, circumference = 2\pi r. Cuboid: volume = lbh, total surface = 2(lb+bh+lh). Cube: volume = l^3, surface = 6l^2. Cylinder: volume = \pi r^2 h, curved surface = 2\pi rh. Take \pi = \frac{22}{7} unless told otherwise. 1 m³ = 1000 litres.

  1. The area of a triangle with base 12 cm and height 9 cm is [1]a108 cm²b54 cm²c21 cm²d27 cm²
  2. The volume of a cube of edge 5 cm is [1]a25 cm³b75 cm³c125 cm³d150 cm³
  3. The circumference of a circle of radius 7 cm, with \pi = \frac{22}{7}, is [1]a22 cmb44 cmc154 cmd49 cm
  4. The total surface area of a cube of edge 4 cm is [1]a16 cm²b64 cm²c96 cm²d24 cm²
  5. The volume of a cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm is [1]a1540 cm³b220 cm³c440 cm³d770 cm³
  6. A tank 2 m × 1 m × 0.5 m holds, when full, [1]a100 litresb500 litresc1000 litresd1500 litres
  7. The area of a trapezium with parallel sides 8 cm and 12 cm and height 5 cm is [1]a50 cm²b100 cm²c40 cm²d60 cm²
  8. If the side of a square is doubled, its area becomes [1]adoublebthree timescfour timesdunchanged
Answers

1. (b) — \frac{1}{2}\times12\times9 = 54 cm².

2. (c) — 5^3 = 125 cm³.

3. (b) — 2\times\frac{22}{7}\times7 = 44 cm.

4. (c) — 6\times4^2 = 96 cm².

5. (a) — \frac{22}{7}\times49\times10 = 1540 cm³.

6. (c) — 1 m³ = 1000 litres.

7. (a) — \frac{1}{2}(8+12)\times5 = 50 cm².

8. (c) — area varies as the square of the side.

5.5 Indices and Algebraic Expressions

Facts. a^m \times a^n = a^{m+n}; \frac{a^m}{a^n} = a^{m-n}; (a^m)^n = a^{mn}; a^0 = 1; a^{-n} = \frac{1}{a^n}; a^{1/2} = \sqrt{a}. (a+b)^2 = a^2+2ab+b^2; (a-b)^2 = a^2-2ab+b^2; a^2-b^2 = (a+b)(a-b).

  1. 2^3 \times 2^4 equals [1]a2^7b2^{12}c4^7d2^{1}
  2. The value of 5^0 + 3^0 is [1]a0b1c2d8
  3. 3^{-2} equals [1]a-9b\frac{1}{9}c-\frac{1}{9}d9
  4. (x+3)^2 expands to [1]ax^2+9bx^2+6x+9cx^2+3x+9dx^2+6x+6
  5. x^2-16 factorises as [1]a(x-4)^2b(x+4)(x-4)c(x+16)(x-1)d(x+4)^2
  6. \frac{a^7}{a^3} equals [1]aa^{10}ba^{21}ca^4da^{4/3}
  7. \sqrt{64} written as a power of 2 is [1]a2^3b2^4c2^6d2^8
  8. If 2^x = 32, then x is [1]a4b5c6d16
Answers

1. (a) — add the indices.

2. (c) — 1+1 = 2.

3. (b) — 3^{-2} = \frac{1}{3^2}.

4. (b) — (a+b)^2 = a^2+2ab+b^2.

5. (b) — difference of two squares.

6. (c) — subtract the indices.

7. (a) — \sqrt{64} = 8 = 2^3.

8. (b) — 2^5 = 32.

5.6 Algebraic Fractions and Equations

Facts. Simplify a fraction by factorising and cancelling common factors — never cancel across a + sign. To add fractions, take the LCM of the denominators. A linear equation keeps its balance: whatever is done to one side is done to the other. The graph of y = mx + c is a straight line of slope m cutting the y-axis at c.

  1. \frac{x^2-9}{x+3} simplifies to [1]ax-3bx+3cx-9dx^2-3
  2. The solution of 3x - 7 = 11 is [1]a4b6c18d\frac{4}{3}
  3. \frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{y} equals [1]a\frac{1}{x+y}b\frac{x+y}{xy}c\frac{2}{xy}d\frac{xy}{x+y}
  4. The slope of the line y = 4x - 5 is [1]a-5b4c\frac{4}{5}d5
  5. The line y = 2x + 3 cuts the y-axis at [1]a(0,2)b(0,3)c(3,0)d(2,0)
  6. If \frac{x}{4} = \frac{9}{6}, then x is [1]a6b8c12d13.5
  7. The value of \frac{2a}{3} - \frac{a}{6} is [1]a\frac{a}{2}b\frac{a}{3}c\frac{3a}{6}d\frac{a}{6}
  8. The solution of \frac{x}{2} + 3 = 7 is [1]a2b5c8d20
Answers

1. (a) — \frac{(x+3)(x-3)}{x+3} = x-3.

2. (b) — 3x = 18, x = 6.

3. (b) — common denominator xy.

4. (b) — the coefficient of x.

5. (b) — put x = 0.

6. (a) — x = \frac{4\times9}{6} = 6.

7. (a) — \frac{4a-a}{6} = \frac{3a}{6} = \frac{a}{2}.

8. (c) — \frac{x}{2} = 4, x = 8.

5.7 Lines, Angles and Plane Figures

Facts. Angles on a straight line add to 180°; angles at a point add to 360°. Vertically opposite angles are equal. With parallel lines, corresponding and alternate angles are equal and co-interior angles are supplementary. Triangle angle sum 180°; exterior angle = sum of the two opposite interior angles. Quadrilateral angle sum 360°. Each interior angle of a regular n-gon is \frac{(n-2)180°}{n}; the exterior angles add to 360°.

  1. Two angles on a straight line are x and 3x. The value of x is [1]a30°b45°c60°d90°
  2. In a triangle two angles are 55° and 65°. The third angle is [1]a50°b60°c70°d120°
  3. Each interior angle of a regular hexagon is [1]a90°b108°c120°d135°
  4. Vertically opposite angles are always [1]asupplementarybcomplementarycequaldright angles
  5. The exterior angle of a triangle is 110° and one opposite interior angle is 45°. The other is [1]a55°b65°c70°d35°
  6. The sum of the exterior angles of any convex polygon is [1]a180°b360°c540°ddepends on the number of sides
  7. A quadrilateral with both pairs of opposite sides parallel but no right angle is a [1]atrapeziumbparallelogramcrectangledkite
  8. Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal and one co-interior angle is 70°. The other is [1]a70°b20°c110°d140°
Answers

1. (b) — 4x = 180°, x = 45°.

2. (b) — 180° - 120° = 60°.

3. (c) — \frac{(6-2)180°}{6} = 120°.

4. (c) — equal.

5. (b) — 110° - 45° = 65°.

6. (b) — always 360°.

7. (b) — a parallelogram.

8. (c) — co-interior angles are supplementary.

5.8 Congruency, Similarity and Solid Objects

Facts. Congruent figures have the same shape and size; tests: SSS, SAS, ASA, RHS. Similar figures have the same shape; corresponding sides are proportional and corresponding angles equal. For a solid: faces F, vertices V, edges E satisfy Euler's relation F + V - E = 2. A cube has 6 faces, 8 vertices, 12 edges; a triangular prism 5 faces, 6 vertices, 9 edges; a square pyramid 5 faces, 5 vertices, 8 edges.

  1. Which test does not prove two triangles congruent? [1]aSSSbSAScAAAdRHS
  2. A cube has edges numbering [1]a6b8c12d16
  3. In two similar triangles, corresponding sides are [1]aequalbproportionalcperpendiculardunrelated
  4. A solid with 5 faces and 6 vertices has edges numbering [1]a8b9c10d12
  5. Two triangles have sides 3,4,5 and 6,8,10 cm. They are [1]acongruentbsimilar but not congruentcneitherdidentical
  6. The number of faces of a square pyramid is [1]a4b5c6d8
  7. If two figures are congruent, they are [1]asimilar as wellbnever similarcsimilar only if squaresdequal in area but not in shape
  8. The RHS test applies only to [1]aequilateral trianglesbright-angled trianglescisosceles trianglesdall triangles
Answers

1. (c) — equal angles fix the shape, not the size.

2. (c) — 12 edges.

3. (b) — proportional.

4. (b) — E = F+V-2 = 5+6-2 = 9.

5. (b) — sides in the ratio 1:2, so similar, not congruent.

6. (b) — four triangular faces and one square base.

7. (a) — congruent figures are similar with ratio 1.

8. (b) — right angle, hypotenuse and one side.

5.9 Coordinates, Transformation, Tessellation, Bearing and Scale Drawing

Facts. In (x,y), x is measured along the horizontal axis. Quadrant signs: I (+,+), II (-,+), III (-,-), IV (+,-). Distance from the origin = \sqrt{x^2+y^2}. Reflection in the x-axis: (x,y) \to (x,-y); in the y-axis: (x,y) \to (-x,y). Translation by \binom{a}{b}: (x,y) \to (x+a, y+b). Rotation through 180° about the origin: (x,y) \to (-x,-y). A regular polygon tessellates if its interior angle divides 360° exactly — so triangle, square and hexagon do. Bearing is measured clockwise from north, written with three figures.

  1. The point (-3, 5) lies in quadrant [1]aIbIIcIIIdIV
  2. The image of (4, -2) after reflection in the x-axis is [1]a(-4,-2)b(4,2)c(-4,2)d(2,4)
  3. The distance of (6,8) from the origin is [1]a10b14c48d\sqrt{14}
  4. Which regular polygon does not tessellate by itself? [1]aequilateral trianglebsquarecregular pentagondregular hexagon
  5. The bearing of due west is [1]a090°b180°c270°d360°
  6. The image of (2,3) under translation \binom{-1}{4} is [1]a(1,7)b(3,-1)c(-2,12)d(1,-1)
  7. On a map of scale 1:50{,}000, 3 cm represents [1]a150 mb1.5 kmc15 kmd150 km
  8. Rotating (5,-1) through 180° about the origin gives [1]a(-5,1)b(5,1)c(-1,5)d(1,-5)
Answers

1. (b) — negative x, positive y.

2. (b) — the sign of y changes.

3. (a) — \sqrt{36+64} = 10.

4. (c) — its interior angle 108° does not divide 360°.

5. (c) — 270° clockwise from north.

6. (a) — (2-1,\,3+4).

7. (b) — 3\times50{,}000 = 150{,}000 cm = 1.5 km.

8. (a) — both signs change.

5.10 Statistics

Facts. Mean = \frac{\sum x}{n}; for a frequency table, mean = \frac{\sum fx}{\sum f}. Median is the middle value of the ordered data — for even n, the mean of the two middle values. Mode is the most frequent value. Range = largest - smallest. In a pie chart, each item's angle = \frac{\text{its frequency}}{\text{total}}\times360°.

  1. The mean of 4, 7, 9, 12 is [1]a7b8c8.5d9
  2. The median of 3, 7, 9, 11, 15 is [1]a7b9c11d10
  3. The mode of 2, 3, 3, 5, 7, 3, 8 is [1]a2b3c5d8
  4. The range of 12, 5, 20, 8 is [1]a8b12c15d20
  5. The median of 4, 8, 10, 14 is [1]a8b9c10d12
  6. In a pie chart of 60 students, the sector for 15 students has an angle of [1]a60°b90°c120°d150°
  7. If the mean of 5 numbers is 12, their sum is [1]a12b17c60d2.4
  8. Which average is most affected by a single very large value? [1]ameanbmediancmodedrange
Answers

1. (b) — \frac{32}{4} = 8.

2. (b) — the third of five ordered values.

3. (b) — 3 occurs three times.

4. (c) — 20-5 = 15.

5. (b) — \frac{8+10}{2} = 9.

6. (b) — \frac{15}{60}\times360° = 90°.

7. (c) — 5\times12 = 60.

8. (a) — the mean uses every value, so an outlier pulls it.

Before you leave this chapter

Eighty items, ten minutes of formula revision. Write the formula list from each facts line on a single card: areas and volumes, interest, indices, polygon angles, transformations, averages. In the last week that card replaces the whole chapter.
